articles.title: Return Of The King
articles.summary: The author recounts an exceptional early morning observation of Jupiter from Fremont Peak, detailing the planet's intricate features like a large brown spot, belt irregularities, and polar granulations visible at 256x magnification. The observer successfully identified all four Galilean moons without aid and expressed immense satisfaction and joy at the detailed view of the gas giant, even as dawn approached.

articles.title: Activities Calendar
articles.summary: This document outlines the activities calendar for June and July, featuring multiple star parties at various locations like Henry Coe, Fremont Peak, and Houge Park. It also schedules monthly general meetings, open board meetings, and beginning astronomy classes covering topics such as telescopes and the moon. Contact information for news and the club's web address are also provided.

articles.title: The Universe On A First Name Basis
articles.summary: Akkana Peck describes her personal challenge in recognizing deep-sky objects by their common names rather than catalog designations. To remedy this, she organized a "named object" observing night on May 3, 1997, meticulously preparing a list of visible objects using an online resource and her star atlases. Despite initial concerns about unpromising weather, conditions at Fremont Peak improved, setting the stage for a successful observing session.

articles.title: Names continued from page 1
articles.summary: This article is a personal observing report detailing a night of deep-sky stargazing. The author tests a new 6" f/4 RFT and an existing 6" f/8 Newtonian, attempting to view various objects like the Rosette Nebula, Antenna Galaxies, Ghost of Jupiter, and the Blinking Planetary, with mixed success and challenges related to identification and conditions. The report also describes interactions with other astronomers, trying out different large telescopes, and the eventual onset of fatigue.

articles.title: Lick Lid Update
articles.summary: Repairs to Lick Observatory's roof are scheduled to begin this summer, following an overwhelming response that raised nearly double the expected funds. This success was largely attributed to internet postings by concerned individuals, and the surplus money will be used for additional safety improvements to the dome.

articles.title: First Annual SJAA Resource Directory
articles.summary: The 'First Annual SJAA Resource Directory' is introduced as a new compilation of local astronomical clubs, organizations, and observatories for San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) members. Designed as a removable reference, it focuses on nearby resources, with potential for future expansion to include national and international listings based on member interest.

articles.title: Astronomical Association of Northern California
articles.summary: The Astronomical Association of Northern California (AANC) is an organization comprising astronomy clubs, businesses, planetaria, and observatories focused on promoting astronomy in Northern California. They originated Astronomy Day, provide resource lists, sponsor conferences and workshops, and host events like the annual "Star-B-Que" at Fremont Peak.

articles.title: Clubs
articles.summary: This document provides a directory of amateur astronomy clubs primarily located in the California Bay Area. It lists contact information, membership numbers, and brief descriptions of each club's unique activities, which include telescope making workshops, administering observatories, hosting star parties, and undertaking large-scale telescope construction projects. The clubs cater to various interests within amateur astronomy.

articles.title: San Francisco Sidewalk Astronomers
articles.summary: The San Francisco Sidewalk Astronomers, founded by John Dobson, is an organization based in San Francisco, CA. The provided content includes contact information for the group, including an address, phone number, and a URL.

articles.title: San Jose Astronomical Assn.
articles.summary: The document provides contact information for the San Jose Astronomical Assn., including details for Jim Van Nuland. It lists a physical address, phone number, email address, and a website URL for the organization.

articles.title: San Mateo Astronomical Society
articles.summary: This document provides basic contact information for the San Mateo Astronomical Society. It lists Ron Cardinale as a contact person, along with a mailing address in San Mateo, California, and a phone number. The society is noted to have 75 members.

articles.title: Santa Cruz Astronomy Club
articles.summary: The Santa Cruz Astronomy Club organizes weekend star parties in the Santa Cruz-Monterey-San Juan Bautista area and holds monthly meetings featuring speakers from local universities and research facilities. The club, with 60 members, provides a contact number for recorded updates and club information.

articles.title: Sonoma County Astronomical Society
articles.summary: The Sonoma County Astronomical Society, based in Santa Rosa, CA, is an organization with 250 members. Contact information for G. Ed Megill is provided, including a postal address and phone number.

articles.title: STARS -- Students Taking Astronomy-Related Subjects
articles.summary: STARS (Students Taking Astronomy-Related Subjects) is a program or group at the City College of San Francisco's Department of Astronomy, led by Darryl Stanford. It currently has 10 members and is associated with a setting that can accommodate up to 50 participants.

articles.title: Stockton Astronomical Society
articles.summary: This document provides contact information for the Stockton Astronomical Society, including a mailing address, phone number for Jeff Baldwin, and states that the society has 100 members.

articles.title: TAC -- The Astronomy Connection
articles.summary: TAC (The Astronomy Connection) is a free, informal internet resource and observing group connecting amateur astronomers. It utilizes email lists to coordinate observing events, share weather updates, and discuss equipment, focusing on bringing people together to observe the night sky without the usual club politics.

articles.title: Tri-Valley Stargazers
articles.summary: This document provides contact and membership information for the Tri-Valley Stargazers, an astronomy club located in Livermore, CA. It lists their postal address, phone, fax, email, website, and indicates they have 189 members.

articles.title: Valley of the Moon Astronomical Society
articles.summary: This document provides contact information for the Valley of the Moon Astronomical Society. It lists Al Heppe as the contact person, along with a mailing address in Glen Ellen, CA, and their phone and fax numbers. The content is solely administrative, offering no details on the society's activities or mission.

articles.title: Western Amateur Astronomers
articles.summary: This document provides contact information for the "Western Amateur Astronomers" group, listing Jack Borde and Stewart Hobson as key contacts. It includes their addresses, phone numbers, and states the group has 32 members.

articles.title: Wragg Canyon Stargazers
articles.summary: The Wragg Canyon Stargazers is a small group of 10 members located in Lake Berryessa, Napa, CA. Judy Spears serves as the primary contact for this stargazing organization.

articles.title: Online Organizations
articles.summary: The article lists and briefly describes several online organizations and platforms dedicated to astronomy discussions and resources. These include the AOL Astronomy Club, sponsored by Sky Publishing and featuring discussion boards and news, Compuserve's astronomy discussion area, and the unmoderated Usenet newsgroups Sci.astro and Sci.astro.amateur. Each entry notes its specific access requirements.

articles.title: Observatories
articles.summary: This document lists contact information for two observatories in California: Chabot Observatory and Science Center in Oakland and Foothill College Observatory in Los Altos. It provides addresses, phone numbers, and URLs for both facilities. The content appears to be part of an observatory directory from a June 1997 publication.

articles.title: Fremont Peak Observatory
articles.summary: Fremont Peak Observatory houses the 30" Challenger Telescope and offers public access on select nights. Contact information for Rick Morales, including a mailing address, phone number, and URL, is provided for inquiries about the observatory.

articles.title: James Lick Observatory
articles.summary: The James Lick Observatory, located on Mount Hamilton, CA, offers regular tours, prominently featuring its 30-inch refractor. The article provides essential contact information, including its postal address, phone number, and official website.

articles.title: Monterey Institute for Research in Astronomy
articles.summary: The Monterey Institute for Research in Astronomy (MIRA) is an organization based in Monterey, CA. The provided document lists its physical address, phone number, and fax number as contact information.

articles.title: Ricard Observatory
articles.summary: The Ricard Observatory, affiliated with the Department of Physics at Santa Clara University in Santa Clara, CA, provides its contact information. This includes a phone number, fax number, and an email address for inquiries.

articles.title: San Francisco State University Observatory
articles.summary: This document provides basic contact and location information for the San Francisco State University Observatory. It lists the department of Physics and Astronomy, its address, phone numbers, and an email address.

articles.title: Sonoma State University Observatory
articles.summary: This document provides essential contact information for the Sonoma State University Observatory, including its departmental affiliation, physical address, phone number, email, and website URL. It serves as a directory entry for those seeking to connect with the observatory.

articles.title: Planitaria
articles.summary: The article 'Planitaria' provides a directory of several planetariums and an earth science center, primarily located in California. It lists contact information, physical addresses, and sometimes seating capacities for institutions like Cabrillo College Planetarium, Chabot College Planetarium, George Clever Planetarium, Diablo Valley College Planetarium, and the Exploratorium.

articles.title: Independence Planetarium
articles.summary: The Independence Planetarium, located at Independence High School in San Jose, CA, is a facility managed by Gail Chaid. It has a seating capacity of 65 and includes contact information for inquiries.

articles.title: Lawrence Hall of Science
articles.summary: The Lawrence Hall of Science, located at the University of California, Berkeley, is an educational institution providing contact details including address, phone, fax, email, and website. It lists its services with codes G, L, M, P, indicating it includes a planetarium with 27 seats.

articles.title: Los Medanos College Planetarium
articles.summary: The Los Medanos College Planetarium, located in Pittsburg, CA, is an educational facility that seats 88 people. It provides a venue for astronomical education and public shows.

articles.title: Minolta Planetarium
articles.summary: The Minolta Planetarium, located at DeAnza College in Cupertino, California, is a facility that seats 170 people. The provided information includes its physical address, contact phone and fax numbers, email, and website URL.

articles.title: Morrison Planetarium
articles.summary: The Morrison Planetarium, located within the California Academy of Sciences in San Francisco's Golden Gate Park, is detailed with its contact information. It provides a seating capacity of 309, along with phone, fax, email, and website details for inquiries.

articles.title: Rosicrucian Planetarium
articles.summary: The Rosicrucian Planetarium, located in San Jose, CA, is an educational facility with a seating capacity of 100. It provides contact information via phone and email. The email address suggests a connection to an Egyptian museum.

articles.title: Santa Rosa Junior College Planetarium
articles.summary: The Santa Rosa Junior College Planetarium is an educational facility located at 1501 Mendocino Ave., Santa Rosa, CA. It offers a viewing space with a seating capacity of 87, and its contact number is 707-527-4371.

articles.title: S.F.S.U. Planetarium
articles.summary: The S.F.S.U. Planetarium, part of the Dept. of Physics and Astronomy at San Francisco State University, provides its contact details including phone number and email address. Located in San Francisco, CA, the facility has a seating capacity of 50.

articles.title: West Valley College Planetarium
articles.summary: The West Valley College Planetarium, located in Saratoga, CA, has a seating capacity of 74 and provides its contact information. This information appeared on page 5 of the June 1997 edition of the 'SJAA Ephemeris' newsletter, a monthly publication of the San Jose Astronomical Association.

articles.title: SWAP Team Results Good
articles.summary: The SJAA Swap Meet and Auction generated $796.15, a slight increase from the previous year, with good attendance noted. The event's financial success indicates its continued popularity, with special thanks extended to participants and auctioneer Jay Freeman. Additionally, David North has been announced as the new Ephemeris Editor.

articles.title: Astro Ads
articles.summary: This "Astro Ads" section features free, non-commercial advertisements for astronomically related products and services. It includes a full-time job opening at Lumicon and a request for an 8" SCT telescope (Meade/Celestron LX-10 type). Instructions are provided for submitting new ads via email or mail, which run for one month unless an extension is requested.

articles.title: Submit
articles.summary: This notice encourages members of the SJAA to submit articles for publication in the monthly Ephemeris newsletter. Submissions should be sent via email to Dave North by the 10th of each month to be included in the following month's issue. Authors are requested to include their name and phone number with their article.

articles.title: Mike Koop
articles.summary: This document, titled "Mike Koop," serves as an inventory and lending log for astronomical equipment, primarily telescopes. It details various scopes by type, borrower, and due date, indicating items that are available, out of service for maintenance, or on a waiting list. Accompanying notes provide updates on equipment status and borrower communication.

articles.title: Officers and Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document lists the officers and board of directors, as well as the Ephemeris staff and Mentoring Program Chairman for an organization. It provides names and phone numbers for individuals holding key positions such as President, Vice President, Secretary, Treasurer, Directors, Editor, and staff responsible for printing and mailing.

articles.title: Activities Committee
articles.summary: This document lists committee members and key contacts for various activities within an organization, including the Activities Committee, Observatory Committee, and specific roles like Observational Astronomy Teacher, School Star Party Chairman, and Telescope Loaner Program coordinator. It provides names and phone numbers for each contact, along with an email for the Web Page contact.

articles.title: Celestial Calendar - June 1997
articles.summary: The Celestial Calendar for June 1997 highlights Comet Hale-Bopp's visibility in the Southern Hemisphere, alongside periodic comets Wild 2 and Encke. The article also announces the discovery of two faint comets by Joe Montani (C/1997 G1 and G2) and Jean Mueller's 12th photographic comet find (C/1997 J1), which is now dimming after perihelion.

articles.title: Ephemerides -- Epoch 2000, 0h UTC
articles.summary: This document provides ephemerides for comets C/1995 O1 (Hale-Bopp) and 81P/Wild 2 for the period of June 1 to July 6, 2000. For each comet, it lists their celestial coordinates (Right Ascension, Declination), solar elongation, and estimated sky magnitude at 0h UTC, intended for observational planning.

articles.title: Orbital Elements -- Epoch 2000.0
articles.summary: This document presents a detailed table of orbital elements for two prominent comets, Hale-Bopp and P/Wild 2, standardized to Epoch 2000.0. It provides specific astronomical data including perihelion date and distance, argument of perihelion, ascending node, inclination, eccentricity, orbital period, and absolute magnitude for each object.

articles.title: TAC June Schedule
articles.summary: This document outlines the TAC's (presumably an astronomy club) schedule for June, featuring various observing opportunities including public nights, star parties, and lunar observing at multiple locations. It notes the need for flexibility due to weather and advises checking mailing lists for updates. Additionally, it provides detailed astronomical ephemeris data for the moon, major planets, the Sun, and twilight times for the month.

articles.title: San Jose Astronomical Association Membership Form
articles.summary: This document is a membership form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), detailing options for new or renewal memberships at a cost of $15 for regular members and $6 for juniors. Members can also add a Sky & Telescope subscription for an additional $27. The form provides instructions for submission via mail to the treasurer, Bob Elsberry, or in person at an SJAA meeting, and includes contact information and a mailing address.
